q: Does the US SEC climate disclosure rule apply to Indian suppliers?
title: SEC climate rule and Indian suppliers
short: No. The SEC climate disclosure rule never placed any duty on suppliers. It covered only companies that file reports with the SEC, it dropped Scope 3 before adoption, and it has been stayed since April 2024 without ever taking effect. An Indian supplier with no US listing has nothing to file under it.
audience: Indian exporters to US listed companies

ul: Indian supplier with no US listing: never in scope. The rule had no supplier or value chain reporting duty.

Indian company with US listed shares that files annual reports with the SEC on Form 20-F: it would have been a registrant itself, with its own climate risk disclosures and, if a large accelerated or accelerated filer and the figures were material, its own Scope 1 and Scope 2. Only Canadian issuers filing on Form 40-F were exempted. With the rule stayed and proposed for rescission, nothing applies today.
Indian subsidiary of a US registrant: not a filer, but its sites sit inside the parent's consolidated Scope 1 and Scope 2, so the parent would have needed its fuel and electricity data.

sections.h: Why Scope 3 matters to this answer
p: The SEC proposal of March 2022 included Scope 3 for some filers, and that was the only part that could have reached outside suppliers. The final rule adopted in March 2024 (Release No. 33-11275) removed Scope 3 entirely, so even in its adopted form no buyer needed supplier emissions to comply with it.

The SEC stayed the rule in April 2024 pending the Iowa v. SEC challenge in the Eighth Circuit, voted in March 2025 to stop defending it, and on 29 May 2026 proposed rescinding it. A final vote is still needed. The step by step history is on the linked status page.

sections.h: If a US customer still asks you for data
p: Ask which rule or programme the request serves, because that decides the year, scopes and format. The reasons US buyers ask are listed on the linked status page. In each case your reply is the same core: Scope 1 and Scope 2 by the GHG Protocol, with factors and sources, for a stated year.

senseible: Senseible prepares Scope 1 and Scope 2 from your invoices and electricity bills, with the factor and source on every line, as a self-declared data pack you can send to a US customer. It does not give legal advice on SEC filing duties.
